newsitem.title: USA: U.S. electronics equipment Q1 sales near $107 bln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. electronics equipment Q1 sales near $107 bln.

text.p: U.S. factory sales of electronics equipment, components and related products rose about eight percent to nearly $107 billion for the first quarter of 1997, according to data released by the Electronic Industries Association.
The report said the most significant increase in sales was in the telecommunications sector where sales gained 13 percent to $15.1 billion compared with $13.3 billion last year.
The only sector to drop was the industrial electronics group, which saw sales lose about one percent to $8.25 billion from $8.33 billion.

The electronic components sales rose five percent to $32.8 billion compared with last year's $31.3 billion. The Consumer electronics sector also saw an increase of eight percent to $2.4 billion compared with $2.2 billion in 1996.

The sales of electromedical equipment saw a nine percent rise to $2.7 billion from $2.5 billion in 1996, the defense communications sector gained six percent to $7.2 billion and the computers and peripherals sector hit $22 billion, an increase of seven percent compared with $20.6 billion last year.
The Electronic Industries Association is the national trade organization representing U.S. electronics manufacturers.
